scope: Corollary 9.3 (Random levels and finite ball probes) of the manuscript “Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising” (preprints/Buffered-comparison-and-stopping-band-resolution-in-critical-Ising-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d5167e3fe5fb85f4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Theorem 9.1 and Corollary 9.2 remain valid when the two contour radii are drawn with a bounded density in a fixed compact rectangle of separated radii lying strictly inside the permitted windows. Different band observations may use independent draws. Their joint data laws converge, including the auxiliary randomness. Fix a countable dense collection of marked rational-walk prototypes in the ambient space b X of Definition 7.3; probe balls are intersected with the admissible-data space Xband. Allow a probe to test whether the data lie within distance r of one prototype, where r is drawn uniformly in a rational interval with closure in (0, 1). For any prescribed ϵ, η, finitely many such probes suffice to obtain the lookup approximation in Corollary 9.2, with adjusted exceptional probability at most ϵ. The finite probe list depends only on the reference local geometry, the radius rectangle, and the requested tolerances. It is independent of the bounded observables and of the size of an ambient buffered array.
